name: Iconography
controls: The drawing style of icons and pictograms on screen, and how icons move and change state.
question: What style should the icons be drawn in, if there are any?
notes: Icon style terms overlap heavily and are used loosely: 'line', 'outline' and 'monoline' are often treated as synonyms. In this taxonomy line icons are the broad stroked category, monoline means one fixed stroke weight with no variation across the whole set, and outline means the stroked version of a filled shape (the pair filled/outline in systems like Material Symbols and Heroicons). Rounded and geometric describe construction and can combine with line or filled rendering. System icons means the platform's own set (SF Symbols on Apple, Material Symbols on Android/Google). Pick at most one style so a video's icons stay consistent; mixing styles is the most common icon mistake. Icon sets on npm or as SVG (Lucide, Phosphor, Heroicons, Tabler, Material Symbols) render directly in HTML; SF Symbols is licensed for Apple platforms only and should be treated as a look reference. Icon motion is a facet; 'animated icons' as a main option means the icons are designed to move (Lottie-style micro-animations).

options.what: Icons drawn primarily with open or closed strokes rather than filled areas.
options.looks: Strokes of 1.5-2px at 24px grid size, open interiors, light visual weight. Lucide, Feather, Tabler Icons, Phosphor (Regular).
options.motion: Draw-on via stroke-dashoffset, line-to-shape fills, subtle rotation.
options.use: SaaS UI, feature lists, explainer diagrams, onboarding.
options.vs: Monoline is a stricter subset (one weight, no variation). Outline icons are the stroked twin of a filled set. Hand-drawn icons are line icons with irregular strokes.
options.prompt: Use line icons from Lucide (or Phosphor Regular): stroke 2px at 24px icon size, scaled so strokes stay 3-4px at 1080p display size (48-64px icons), round caps and joins, currentColor. One stroke weight across all icons; no fills except a single accent dot.

options.what: Line icons with one uniform stroke weight across every line, curve and icon in the set.
options.looks: Perfectly even strokes, consistent terminals, no tapering; icons read as one system. Lucide and Feather are monoline; many custom brand sets are too.
options.motion: Continuous draw-on of a single path, path-to-path morphs that keep stroke weight.
options.use: Technical and minimalist brands, infographics, wayfinding-style explainers.
options.vs: Line icons may vary weight between primary and detail strokes; monoline never does. Outline icons are defined by pairing with a filled version, not by weight.
options.prompt: Draw every icon as monoline: one stroke weight (3px at 1080p for 56px icons) with round caps, no fills, no tapered or variable strokes, identical corner radius (2px) everywhere; set vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke so scaling never changes weight.

options.what: The stroked version of a filled icon shape, typically part of a paired outline/filled set used for inactive vs active states.
options.looks: Closed contours tracing the silhouette of the filled version, 1.5-2px strokes. Material Symbols (Outlined), Heroicons Outline, SF Symbols (default vs .fill).
options.motion: Outline-to-filled fill transition as a state change (tab selected, liked, saved).
options.use: Product UI tab bars and toolbars, state changes in UI demos.
options.vs: Line icons can be open strokes with no filled counterpart; outline icons trace a filled shape so they can switch to it. Monoline is about weight, outline about construction.
options.prompt: Use outline icons from Heroicons Outline or Material Symbols Outlined (weight 400, grade 0) at 48-64px on 1080p; when an icon becomes active, switch to its filled twin by cross-fading or clip-wiping the filled version over 200ms ease power2.out.

options.what: Icons rendered as solid silhouettes with interior detail knocked out.
options.looks: Heavy, high-contrast shapes readable at small sizes and far distances. Heroicons Solid, Material Symbols (Filled), Font Awesome Solid, Phosphor Fill.
options.motion: Scale pops, color changes, bounce on state change.
options.use: Active UI states, mobile apps, small-size legibility, bold social graphics.
options.vs: Glyphs are single-color filled icons designed to sit in text or font files; filled icons are the general rendering style. Outline icons are their stroked twins.
options.prompt: Use filled icons (Phosphor Fill or Heroicons Solid) at 48-72px on 1080p in one solid color with interior details as knockouts; place them on 96-120px rounded containers (radius 24px) in a tinted brand color for contrast.

options.what: Single-color, compact symbols designed to sit inline with text like characters.
options.looks: Tiny, dense silhouettes aligned to the text baseline and cap height. Material Symbols and Font Awesome ship as icon fonts; SF Symbols align to San Francisco text.
options.motion: Minimal: color changes and inline replacement alongside text.
options.use: Inline in captions, buttons, labels, lower thirds, tiny UI chrome.
options.vs: Filled icons are standalone graphics; glyphs are scaled and aligned to type. 'Glyph' also means any character in a font, so usage varies.
options.prompt: Render icons as glyphs inline with text: same color as the text, sized to 1.0-1.2x cap height, baseline aligned, 0.3em gap; use Material Symbols as a variable icon font (wght matching the text weight) so icons and text share stroke weight.

options.what: Icons drawn in two tones, typically a primary shape plus a lighter secondary layer.
options.looks: A solid or stroked main form over a translucent (20-40% opacity) or tinted secondary fill. Phosphor Duotone, Font Awesome Duotone.
options.motion: Secondary layer offsets or fills in after the primary; two-step reveals.
options.use: Marketing sites, feature grids, SaaS product pages, dashboards.
options.conveys: Polish, depth without 3D, brand color presence.
options.vs: Duotone photography maps an image to two colors; duotone icons layer two tones in a vector icon. Filled icons use one tone.
options.prompt: Use duotone icons (Phosphor Duotone): primary strokes or shapes in the brand color at 100%, secondary fill in the same color at 25% opacity. Reveal the secondary layer 120ms after the primary, sliding 4px into registration, ease power2.out.

options.what: Icons with rounded corners, caps and joins throughout.
options.looks: Soft corners (2-4px radius at 24px), round caps, friendly geometry. Material Symbols Rounded, Phosphor, SF Symbols (inherently rounded joins).
options.motion: Soft springy pops, squash on tap, gentle morphs.
options.use: Consumer apps, health, family, finance for beginners.
options.vs: Geometric icons use strict circles and squares and can be sharp; rounded is about softening terminals and corners, independent of line or fill.
options.prompt: Use Material Symbols Rounded (or Phosphor) with round caps and joins, corner radius 25% of stroke-to-edge distance; pair with pill buttons and rounded cards. Animate state changes with a 1.15 scale overshoot, ease back.out(2), 300ms.

options.what: Icons built strictly from primitive shapes (circles, squares, triangles) on a tight grid.
options.looks: Pure primitives, precise 45 and 90 degree angles, strong symmetry, often sharp corners. Material Symbols Sharp, custom Bauhaus-style sets.
options.motion: Primitive-to-primitive morphs, modular assembly (pieces fly in and lock), rotations by 90 degrees.
options.use: Tech, architecture, data products, Swiss-style and Bauhaus-influenced brands.
options.vs: Rounded icons soften everything; technical icons add dimension lines and detail. Geometric is about construction from primitives.
options.prompt: Build icons only from circles, squares, rectangles and 45-degree triangles on a 24-unit grid with 2-unit strokes, sharp corners (Material Symbols Sharp style). Assemble each icon on entry: primitives slide in from 40px out and lock, 350ms ease power3.out, stagger 50ms.

options.what: The platform's own icon set used exactly as in the operating system or design system.
options.looks: SF Symbols on iOS/macOS, Material Symbols on Android and Google products, Fluent System Icons on Windows.
options.motion: Native state animations: SF Symbols bounce, replace and variable-color effects; Material's fill axis.
options.use: Realistic product demos, device mockups, platform-native app launches.
options.conveys: Authenticity, native fit, 'this is really how it works'.
options.vs: Custom brand icons are drawn for the brand; system icons are the platform default. Glyph describes rendering; system describes source.
options.prompt: Use the target platform's system icons exactly (Material Symbols for Android/web; for Apple UI match SF Symbols' look with a licensed-for-web equivalent such as Phosphor Regular), at the platform's native sizes scaled 2x for 1080p, with native state animations only.

options.what: An icon set drawn specifically for a brand, carrying its shape language, weights and colors.
options.looks: Distinctive corner treatments, brand-specific stroke weight, color accents, sometimes a signature detail repeated across icons.
options.use: Brand films, marketing sites, product launches from design-led companies.
options.vs: System icons are borrowed; custom brand icons are proprietary. Pictograms are larger and more illustrative.
options.prompt: Draw a custom icon set that inherits the brand's shape language: same corner radius as the logo, stroke weight matched to the wordmark's stem thickness, one brand-color accent detail per icon in the same position. Keep 6-10 icons consistent on a 48-unit grid.

options.what: Larger, more illustrative symbols that depict a concept or action, often with simplified figures.
options.looks: Simplified scenes or figures, filled or bold line, more detail than a UI icon; wayfinding lineage (AIGA/DOT symbols, Olympic pictograms, Otl Aicher). IBM Design Language pictograms.
options.motion: Small narrative loops: a figure walks, a package moves, parts assemble.
options.use: Explainers, infographics, onboarding steps, wayfinding, signage-style information.
options.vs: Icons are compact UI controls; pictograms communicate a concept on their own at larger sizes. Spot illustrations are more detailed and stylistic still.
options.prompt: Use pictograms at 160-280px on 1080p: bold 6-8px strokes or solid fills, simplified round-headed figures, one accent color per pictogram, drawn on a consistent 64-unit grid. Give each a 1-2s micro-loop (one part moves) that explains the step.

options.what: Icons with irregular, sketch-like strokes that show the hand.
options.looks: Wobbly lines, uneven weight, overshooting corners, marker or pencil texture.
options.motion: Write-on draw paths, boiling lines (2-3 alternating drawings at 8-12fps), jittery pops.
options.use: Education, community products, creative tools, friendly explainers, whiteboard-style videos.
options.vs: Line icons are precise vectors; hand-drawn icons are intentionally imperfect. Doodle mascots extend the same look to characters.
options.prompt: Draw icons with irregular 3-5px strokes (variable width, overshooting corners, slightly open joins), black or ink color on a light ground. Draw them on with stroke-dashoffset over 600ms, then boil: swap between 3 slightly different path versions every 3 frames.

options.what: Icons styled as die-cut stickers with a thick white border and slight shadow.
options.looks: Filled colorful icon, 6-10px white outline following the silhouette, soft drop shadow, occasional peel or tilt.
options.motion: Slap-on (scale overshoot plus rotation), peel reveals, wobble.
options.use: Social-first content, youth brands, messaging apps, creator tools.
options.vs: Emoji-like icons are glossy expressive faces and objects; sticker icons are defined by the die-cut border.
options.prompt: Render icons as die-cut stickers: saturated flat fill, 8px white stroke around the silhouette (paint-order stroke), box-shadow 0 6px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.18), rotated -8 to 8 degrees. Slap on: scale 1.4 to 1 and rotation -20 to final over 300ms, ease back.out(2.5).

options.what: Icons rendered as lit three-dimensional objects.
options.looks: Volumetric forms, soft studio lighting, glossy or matte plastics, gradients from lighting rather than paint; usually pre-rendered images or Three.js.
options.motion: Slow turntable rotation, float and bob, bounce landings, camera dolly past.
options.use: Landing pages, app launches, Web3, feature cards, social ads.
options.vs: Clay icons are a matte, soft 3D subset; skeuomorphic icons imitate real materials in 2D or 3D with detailed realism.
options.prompt: Use 3D icons rendered with soft studio lighting (key top-left, rim light right), glossy plastic in two brand tints, at 200-320px on 1080p. Float them: y +-8px over 3s, ease sine.inOut, yoyo, plus rotationY +-10 degrees on offset timing.

options.what: Soft, matte 3D icons that look modeled from clay or soft plastic.
options.looks: Puffy rounded forms, pastel palette, matte surfaces, soft ambient occlusion, no hard specular highlights.
options.motion: Squashy bounces, gentle wobble, pops with squash and stretch.
options.use: Consumer apps, fintech for young audiences, onboarding, friendly SaaS.
options.vs: 3D icons can be glossy and hard; clay is always matte and soft. 'Claymorphism' is informal trend vocabulary.
options.prompt: Render icons as matte clay: pastel fills, fully rounded edges (no sharp corners), soft inner highlight (inset 6px 6px 12px rgba(255,255,255,0.6)) and inner shade (inset -6px -6px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.12)), soft contact shadow. Bounce in with squash scaleY 0.85 on landing.

options.what: Icons that imitate real-world objects and materials in detail: leather, metal, glass, paper.
options.looks: Textures, bevels, reflections, stitching, realistic lighting; the pre-2013 iOS era look.
options.motion: Physical: dials rotate, switches flip, lids open, light glints.
options.use: Retro-tech nostalgia, hardware-like product metaphors, audio tools, premium detailed apps.
options.vs: 3D icons are stylized volumes; skeuomorphic icons copy a specific real object and material. Neumorphism is a separate soft-shadow UI trend, not skeuomorphism.
options.prompt: Draw icons as realistic objects: real material textures (brushed metal, leather, glass), 1px highlight bevels, top-down key light, contact shadows. Animate physically: a dial rotates 90 degrees with inertia (ease power3.out, 600ms), a toggle flips with a 2-frame settle.

options.what: Glossy, expressive, full-color icons in the visual language of emoji sets.
options.looks: Full-color gradients, soft highlights, rounded forms, faces and expressive objects. Noto Emoji (Google, open), Microsoft Fluent Emoji (3D and flat, open source), Apple Color Emoji (proprietary).
options.motion: Reaction bursts, float-ups, pop-ins, facial expression swaps.
options.use: Social content, messaging and community features, reactions, casual explainers.
options.vs: Sticker icons have die-cut borders; emoji-like icons borrow emoji rendering and expressiveness.
options.prompt: Use Microsoft Fluent Emoji (3D or Flat, open source) or Noto Emoji at 96-160px on 1080p for reactions and expressive markers. Burst them upward: y 0 to -200px with random x drift +-40px, scale 0.5 to 1.2, opacity to 0 over 1.2s, stagger 60ms.

options.what: Precise, engineering-style icons with fine lines, detail and schematic cues.
options.looks: Thin 1-1.5px lines, dimension marks, crosshairs, cutaways, monospace labels, blueprint or CAD feel.
options.motion: Precise draw-ons, measurement lines extending, exploded-view separations.
options.use: Hardware, infrastructure, developer tools, security, engineering products.
options.vs: Geometric icons are simple primitives; technical icons add schematic detail and annotation.
options.prompt: Draw technical icons with 1.5px strokes at 64px on 1080p, square caps, small crosshairs and tick marks, a 4px corner bracket frame, monospace labels at 14-16px. Draw on with stroke-dashoffset in 400ms, ease power1.inOut, then extend dimension lines.

options.what: Icons designed with built-in micro-animations that express their meaning (a bell rings, a trash lid opens).
options.looks: Usually line or duotone base with animation baked in; delivered as Lottie JSON or SVG with timelines. LottieFiles, Lordicon, Google's animated Material Symbols.
options.motion: Short 0.5-1.5s meaning-carrying loops or one-shots triggered on state changes.
options.use: Feature highlights, UI demos, onboarding, notification moments.
options.vs: Any icon can be animated; this option means the icon style is designed around its motion. The motion facet describes the specific motion.
options.prompt: Give every icon a one-shot micro-animation that acts out its meaning in 500-900ms (bell swings +-15 degrees twice, trash lid lifts 20 degrees, check draws on), triggered on its entry. Keep all icons in one base style and seek-safe on the timeline (no autoplaying Lottie loops).

options.what: One icon's shape transforms smoothly into another (play to pause, menu to close).
options.prompt: Morph between icon paths with MorphSVGPlugin over 300-450ms, ease power2.inOut; match point counts or use shapeIndex so the in-between never tangles; keep stroke weight constant.

options.what: Strokes are drawn progressively along their paths.
options.prompt: Set stroke-dasharray to the path length and animate stroke-dashoffset from length to 0 over 400-700ms, ease power1.inOut, staggering sub-paths by 60ms; fills (if any) fade in after the strokes.

options.what: An outline icon fills with color, or a fill drains away.
options.prompt: Clip-wipe the filled version over the outline version bottom-to-top (clip-path inset from 100% to 0) over 250ms ease power2.out; reverse for deselect.

options.what: The icon spins to indicate process or change.
options.prompt: Rotate 90 or 180 degrees for state change (300ms, ease back.out(1.6)); for loading, rotate 360 degrees continuously at 1 turn per 1s, ease none.

options.what: The icon pops with an overshoot to draw attention.
options.prompt: Scale 1 to 1.25 to 1 over 350ms (ease back.out(3)) or y -12px and back with ease bounce.out; use once per icon for attention, never looping.

options.what: The icon switches between states (off/on, empty/liked) with a transitional flourish.
options.prompt: Transition the icon between states in 200-300ms: swap outline to filled, change color to the active accent, scale 0.85 to 1.1 to 1, optional 6-particle burst for positive states like like or save.

options.what: A line or stroke expands into a solid shape or container.
options.prompt: Start with a single 3px stroke; morph or scale it into a filled rounded rectangle or circle over 500ms ease power3.inOut, then reveal content inside.

options.what: An icon expands into the interface or screen it represents.
options.prompt: Use Flip to scale the icon's container into the full UI panel over 700ms ease power3.inOut; cross-fade the icon out and the UI content in during the middle 40% of the move.

options.what: Icons converge or morph into the brand logo as an ending.
options.prompt: Gather 3-6 feature icons toward center over 600ms ease power3.in, morph the final shape into the logomark with MorphSVGPlugin over 400ms, then reveal the wordmark with a 300ms masked slide.
